Zac: Zac is the name of a bright red balloon at a birthday party that was full of air about 7 hrs ago, but now has a few slack wrinkles all over it. A nice guy. A nice balloon. Zac is (and was) a splendid mischief maker and when it counted he was very good. Barely a malicious bone in his body.
Zacarih: You know that thing chickens do after you lop their heads off? It's called the Zacarih Dance, and luckily you don't need to be Einstein to do it.
Zachary: The poor bastard. His parents gave him that name because they thought it would be a cool thing to do, but they might as well have called him Seventy Cents Worth of Chips, as no one can ever take him seriously.
Zachery: Yep, you might want to check out Zachary, Zachery. What was ommitted in his description however, and it applies to you too, is that you are both decent, happy young men. So well done on that front, anyway.
Zack: Fruit juice. 100% organic with no added sugar.
Zackary: Serious? Zackary? Don't be bloody stupid. The last job interview he turned up to he wore a pale blue safari suit. He didn't really want the job of course, and so dressed in a way that he hoped would convince his potential employers at the accounting firm that he was slightly batty. It totally back-fired. They thought his colour and verve implied a certain kind of joie de vivre, and that he'd bring a breath of fresh air into the office. They employed him on the spot. Now he has to work a 9 to 5 job and doesn't he love it? Not! Although, his employers were right. He has definitely freshened up the place and people are happier with him around.
Zade: Quiet and care-free, Zade generally lets the girl make the first move but we have no idea about the direction of his life. When he begins to move toward some ambition or other can you let us know? Thanks. Management.
Zai: No, he's not a Greek symbol in mathematics. He's a polite and independent young man who quite unconcsiously endeavours to keep his life simple.
Zaiden: "Come on, hurry up! Give me that adrenalin, quick!.......Zaiden, are you awake? You need to go to school, mate. Wake up."…….
Zain: He's not the leader but he's definitely a member of the gang.
Zak: Zak looks quite manly but he is putty in the hands of any woman.
Zamika: Loveable and completely unconventional, Zamika is always relaxed, and no matter how stressed or panicked those around him appear to be. It’s a product of having an unyielding sense of humour, courtesy of a ridiculous mother, combined with an ingrained sense of wrong and right.
Zan: As the world’s most honest snake charmer, Zan loves a challenge.
Zanda:
“Hang on, hang on,” the army Major says to the General. “You're going to put Zanda in charge of the mission into that Sudanese strong-hold? Are you out of your mind? Do you remember how he won the war games battle? He hired a bunch of girls and got them to put on bikinis, before sneaking them into the opposing forces HQ tent. What do you think you're doing? He doesn't take responsibility for himself and he'll get everyone killed!” The General smiles and picks up his drink, takes a sip and places it back on the table.
“Major,” he says, “this is Africa, and this is a wild part of the world. Do you think normal operational procedures are going to work here? I tell you, if Zanda does his job well he'll absolutely prevail, no one will get shot and he might even end up becoming a local warlord. Then, peace will be ours. I don't care how he does it.”
Zandah: Zandah is a slightly watered-down version of his twin brother, Zanda, so you better go check him out. The pointless 'h' at the end of his name is the culprit, but that's another story.
Zander: A respectful young man who rarely shouts at people. Indeed, confrontations aren't really his thing and he'll go to huge lengths to avoid these situations, be it a public setting or not.
Zane: Zane is the name of an expensive pane of glass in a plush modern apartment. He lets in all the winter sun and keeps out the summer heat, and all that, and he does it pretty easily. And he looks good. Yep. That’s about it. He looks good.
Zatlin:
Can you imagine Zatlin training for the infantry? On gattling gun training day he’d get on the thing, point it straight up into the sky and let go with everything, disregarding both his screaming sergeant, barely audible above the din, as well as the target at the end of the paddock that he’s supposed to be shooting at. When the ammo runs out, ending everyone’s day early, smoke is coming off the death machine, the sergeant is fuming and Zatlin is beaming the biggest smile anyone has ever seen. “Can you imagine what that’d look like at night?” he asks, looking up at the sky and wondering where all those machine gun bullets are right now. His sergeant looks at him and then points back to the barracks. “Son, I’m kicking you out of the army.”
Let’s face it, is a win-win for everyone.
Zavier: We suspect all this predictive text rubbish is the cause, but phenotypic spelling is rapidly taking over the world – I mean, just look at L_ah’s parents – but Zavier’s folks did a bit better than hers. Zavier is decent young fellow. Like his distant cousin Sam, Zavier rarely has a nasty bone in his body. Indeed, the only times we’ve seen him really pissed off is when he is lost.
Zayn: While not a boofhead, Zayn is a little lazy. His smile helps him here but no one is a teenager forever….we think!
Zeano: Zeano is actually a serene pesonality. Yeah, he carries on with the boys and talks his measure of shit, but get him away from all that and he's quite the introspective man. He's definitely more sensitive than he looks.
Zebedee: I'm terribly sorry but you're on the wrong floor. Name Theories for Cartoon Characters is two floors up. Good luck, but I do like the outfit, Zebedee. You've obviously gone to a lot of effort and for that we commend you.
Zebulan: Like a 3-D maze with a mind of its own, Zebulan is a perpexling individual. He likes to get to the bottom of things and he's no idiot. Sure, he has a ridiculous-sounding name but he is unbothered by either your reaction or anyone else's. Z is his own man, and if you're strategising for war then I'd get him down here in the bunker to meet the top brass, pronto.
Zeke: Zeke is a clone pumped out of a cyborg factory. You can pick them from the way they walk (they kind of saunter along without using their arms) and from their earrings. Invariably, they have these huge bone-type circles that become enlarged over time. Indeed, if you ever meet a 'Zeke' and his giant bone-type earrings are missing you should call the Cyborg Police, corner him and DO NOT let him escape. The last thing we need walking around are robots more self-aware and intelligent than we are.
Zemaras: Lawyer or car salesman, and many might question what the difference is. It’s all about the perceived veneer, right? Is he capable of badgering a witness or a mechanically naive lady? You’re damn right he is.
Zen: Your local car mechanic. And in a million years he'd never rip you off. But he will charge at the going rate.
Zenon:
Zenon is a decent, friendly young man but, honestly, why does it take him so long to tell you the time? 
In fact, why does it take him so long to do anything you ask him? Zenon, are your batteries charged up, or what?
Zep: Yep, Zep is in the building so we can commence. He's been off getting a few vital items that, in the end, meant that the show could go ahead. Zep knows everyone, you see. If you need props, money, perhaps you need a hand to get that bloody fridge upstairs? Zep will be round in a flash and he'll incorporate these tasks into the rest of his day rather seamlessly.
Zephyr: Hang on, where is he? Is he over there? Yes? Oh, no, he's gone again! Zephyr, where are you boy? Christ, how many girls have you kissed this week? You better wear a condom lad. And you do realise that you might need to work once in a while if you want to buy that new surfboard, yeah?
Zepplin: Zepplin is full of hot air sometimes, but he doesn't take himself seriously enough to be an arrogant man. Sure, he knows he has a silly name but he likes it. We all do. The result is a fellow born to mingle with people, stranger and friend alike. His views and opinions are actually quite astute.
Zepulon: One of very few men in the Kingdom who holds his farts back until he's inside a packed lift.
Zetland: No, he’s not an airship and he’s not all that courageous, really. Having said all that he should exercise more than he does, although his love of comic books, even here in adulthood, means that he can’t really get outside that much anyway. Zetland, you need to think about that.
Zhaedyn: They say women start to arrive into their real personality at 27, men at 30. This may or not be true as a given generalisation, but it's pretty much on the money for young Zhaedyn. Shyer than you think, it'll take him a while to find his feet, but he has a kind heart and he's not as slack as people seem to presume. If you know one, once in a while just take the time to remind him to ignore his peers and follow his heart. He’ll be right and yes, his parents are fucking idiots.
Zhivago: Bloody Zhivago. We gave him a job in the foreign office as some kind of diplomat, you see, and he spent all his time (and our money) wining and dining the gorgeous wives of these foreign government officials. In itself that wouldn't have been a problem (he opened many doors and allowed trade relations with some of our more testy neighbours to remain in excellent shape) but all these women fell in love with him. We don't know if it was his conversation or his smile, or the way he asks questions. We'd ask him, of course, but he vanished with the wife of a visiting foreign secretary didn't he! We dealt with that scandal easily enough but the trouble is, Zhivago knows how to disappear. God knows where they are now...
Zion: Not a patch on his female counterpart, Zion's greatest ambition is to get his latest tattoo coloured-in.
Zobie: Zobie, we commend you on your aspirations but positions of meaningful authority aren't your deal. Your leadership skills aren't the best, and the last thing this boat needs is a skipper who will abandon the helm at the first sign of peril. Stay on land.
Zoc: His name sounds like an axe cutting into a heavy log and this isn’t far from his measure. The quickness of his title conceals the lengths that he’ll go to, to elucidate the truth. And that’s why he’s here. What a tremendous, searching individual.
Zoran:
Zoran says yes more than he says no. His whole demeanor is one of a company CEO who wears a suit only to give the impression that he's in charge, and who takes every opportunity to get out the door and either rush to lunch (or the gold course). Unless of course there is a crisis and he actually needs to make crucial decisions, which he will and can, and here in lies the rub. Zoran is a skilled and compassionate leader -  tough but loving - but really, he'd rather just go fishing than put on this show of being the boss. Plenty of friends. A good dad. 

That make sense?...
Zorba: This man lives a life that is akin to a male detective character in a cartoon book. At one stage he had $80,000 in a shoebox in his bedroom. No one knows how he accrued it – Zorba seems to find himself in these sorts of situations all the time, although he has a lot more stashed in a Swiss bank account – but I suppose it’s the natural result of being quite a remarkable personality (not to mention another sexual deviant).
Zvonka: Yaar, Zvonka from the Eastern block. And yaar, Zvonka is bonka. (No, not bonking, you idiot. BONKERS!!!)
Zyg: The transparent charlatan. By his very nature he gets away with everything under the sun. He’d make a good arms dealer, convincing everyone why he is needed in the world. But, he’s smart, he’s charismatic and he knows how to play to the crowd.
